operational_milestone_notes: Alcasa Line 1 Phase II expansion completed to 22.5 kt/yr nominal capacity. Alumina imported.
Alcasa domestic and Andean Pact exports.
Alcasa full Line 1 capacity utilization.
Venalum incorporated (CVG 80% with Japanese consortium Showa Denko Kobe Steel Marubeni Sumitomo 20%).
Carlos Andres Perez administration initiates Fifth National Plan; oil nationalization revenues fund heavy industry.
Alcasa Phase III expansion begins ramping up toward 50-55 kt.
Construction begins on Venalum smelter complex at Matanzas (Puerto Ordaz).
Alcasa Line 2 operations; Interalumina established to build domestic alumina refinery.
Venalum formally inaugurated on June 10 1978; initial reduction cells commissioned.
Venalum potlines 1-2 ramp-up; Bauxiven founded to develop Los Pijiguaos bauxite deposit.
Venalum potlines 3-4 commissioned; total primary aluminum output exceeds 300 kt.
Smelters leverage Guri Stage I hydroelectric power; export orientation to Japan and US.
Latin American debt crisis builds; aluminum exports critical non-oil FX earner.
Viernes Negro currency devaluation (4.30 to floating Bs/USD); Interalumina refinery commissioned.
Alcasa Line 3 expansion ramps up; Interalumina expands alumina production to 800 kt.
Interalumina achieves domestic alumina self-sufficiency; imports eliminated.
Guri Dam Final Stage (Stage II) inaugurated raising generating capacity to 10000 MW.
Commercial bauxite mining commences at Los Pijiguaos (Bauxiven); barged down Orinoco River.
Venalum Line 5 expansion (V Line) begins testing; Alcasa Line 4 ramp-up.
El Gran Viraje IMF package and Caracazo social unrest; Venalum Line 5 fully operational.
Venezuela solidifies position as largest installed primary aluminum capacity in Latin America.
Los Pijiguaos bauxite reaches 3.0 Mt extraction; rail-to-barge transfer at El Jobal.
Feb 4 and Nov 27 coup attempts; primary smelter operations continue uninterrupted.
Impeachment of Carlos Andres Perez; interim Velasquez government.
Banco Latino collapse; CVG Bauxilum created via merger of Bauxiven and Interalumina.
Rafael Caldera Agenda Venezuela; planned privatization of CVG aluminum complex initiated.
Aluminum privatization auctions fail repeatedly due to high debt liabilities and labor conditions.
All-time historical production peak of Venezuelan primary aluminum (642 kt).
Final aluminum privatization auction collapses; election of Hugo Chavez in December.
New Constitution of the Bolivarian Republic; state retention of basic industries affirmed.
Consolidation under CVG corporate governance; Reynolds minority stake bought out.
High global primary aluminum prices; Venalum operates near nominal capacity.
April 2002 coup attempt and December 2002-February 2003 general strike; smelters maintain base operations.
CADIVI exchange controls introduced; CVG export revenues increasingly redirected.

USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 623.5 kt; Alcasa cogestion (worker co-management) experiment.

USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 610-615.7 kt; Alcasa produced 180680 metric tons.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 610.0 kt; SIDOR renationalized; CVG cash flows redirected to FONDEN.
Severe El Nino drought at Guri Dam; Chavez orders forced power curtailment; Alcasa Line 1 permanently shuttered.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 400.0 kt; nationwide electricity emergency; potline cell de-rating.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 330.0 kt; Venalum produces 260.7 kt; Alcasa down to 69.3 kt.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 208.0 kt; Venalum 152.4 kt; Bauxilum alumina shortage starves potlines.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 186.0 kt; Chavez death and election of Nicolas Maduro; FX crunch.
USGS Table 1: Venalum drops to 109.5 kt (25% capacity); acute shortage of carbon anodes and cryolite.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 119.1-119.7 kt; Alcasa 28.5 kt; Venalum 91.2 kt; Bauxilum drops below 1 Mt bauxite.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 86.0 kt; acute electricity crisis; Guri water level reaches critical low.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 80.0 kt; US financial sanctions (EO 13808); loss of trade credit lines.
USGS Table 1: Bauxite 0 kt alumina 0 kt; Venalum produces 60.2 kt with <80 cells active; hyperinflation.
March 7-12 nationwide blackouts; potlines freeze and solidify molten metal; Alcasa destroyed; Venalum shutdown.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 20.0 kt (e); dismantling of Alcasa Lines 3 and 4 reduction cells.
USGS Table 1: Primary aluminum 20-38.3 kt; Venalum operates 145 reactivated cells (8.9% capacity).
USGS Table 1 (Advance Release): Primary aluminum 47.0 kt (e); Bauxilum refinery 80.0 kt (e).
Venalum operates isolated potlines (<10% capacity); sporadic spot ingot sales.
Trace industrial production; negotiations with international traders for smelter refurbishment.
Baseline trace output; Alcasa primary smelting permanently ceased; Venalum minimal operations.
Structural baseline projection (<5% installed capacity); primary aluminum industry requires >$1.6B overhaul.
